_readme: Reference cases for the Surge/Swab module (js/surge-swab.js: closed-pipe Burkhardt velocity, Herschel-Bulkley slot laminar solution, Bourgoyne/API 13D turbulent branch, BHA OD steps). Run: npm run test:surgeswab
All lengths ft, diameters in, mud ppg, PV cp, YP lb/100ft2, speed ft/min, pressures psi (imperial = QuackPlan canonical).
IMPORTANT: no truly public, downloadable PWD trip time-series exists (see 'unavailable' below). The numeric cases here are
published SIMULATION outputs (Landmark WellPlan, Pegasus SurgeMOD, textbook hand-calcs) that were themselves checked against
field practice. Use them as sanity/regression targets, not as pass/fail truth. Field-measured (PWD) sources are listed with what
they contain so you can key the numbers in by hand if you have library access.

cases.source: Salih, Hadi, Al Saba (2024) 'Analysis of Surge and Swab ECD of Herschel Bulkley Fluids in Rumaila Iraqi Oil Field', Iraqi J. Chem. Pet. Eng. 25(1) 141-153, https://doi.org/10.31699/IJCPE.2024.1.14 (open access, Table 2 + Table 3)
notes: Well R-A, 12 1/4in section. 13 3/8in casing shoe at 649 m (ID assumed 12.415in, 68 lb/ft); open hole 12.25in to 1957 m (bit at 1957 m MD, opposite Hartha thief zone).

Mud 9.51 ppg gel/polymer WBM. HB: tau_y = 12 lb/100ft2, n = 0.6, K = 0.03 in the paper's unit 'lb.s^n/ft2' = 3.0 lb.s^n/100ft2 (the only reading that gives a physical mud; the reference script uses that). Bingham PV 20 / YP 12 is a rough equivalent used as a second column.
Trip speed given as sec/stand; 30 sec/stand = 60 m/min in the paper => stand = 30 m = 98.4 ft => v_ftmin = 5906 / t_sec.
TVD assumed = MD (paper gives MD only; S-shaped well, section is shallow). ECD 'at bit' = ECD referenced to bit TVD.
Closed-ended values are the right comparison for QuackPlan (Burkhardt closed-pipe). Open-ended values shown for context.

cases.source: Same paper as above, section 3.2 + Table 6 (9 5/8in casing run through the 12 1/4in open hole, same mud)
notes: 9.625in casing (ID 8.681), float collar/shoe OD 10.396in, shoe at 1680 m MD (5512 ft). Hole: 13 3/8in casing to 649 m, 12.25in OH below.
Annular clearance 12.25-9.625 = 2.625in => this is the narrow-annulus stress case for the model.
Text values: closed-ended surge ECD at 1680 m for 200 -> 20 sec/stand = 10.4 -> 13.0 ppg (FG 13.81). Open-ended at TD 200 -> 10 sec/stand: surge 10.26 -> 15.2, swab 8.76 -> 3.82 ppg.
Closed vs open at 100 sec/stand: 11.03 vs 10.83 ppg; at 55 sec/stand: 11.69 vs 11.41 ppg (run-depth analysis at TD).
Stand length assumed 30 m as in the drill-pipe case (paper keeps 'sec/stand'); if WellPlan used single joints (~12 m) the speeds are 2.5x lower.

cases.source: Salih & Hadi (2024) 'Estimation of Surge and Swab Pressures While Tripping for Minimizing Excessive Drilling Problems', Iraqi Geological Journal 57(1D) 174-200, https://igj-iraq.org/igj/index.php/igj/article/view/2124 (open access, Table 2, Table 5, Fig. 14)
cases.kind: simulation (Landmark WellPlan DYNAMIC/transient model) — magnitudes are far above steady-state; treat as an upper bound, NOT a target
notes: Vertical well R-A, 8.5in production section. 9 5/8in casing (ID 8.681) to 1942 m; 8.5in OH to 3290 m.
Mud 9.96 ppg WBM, Bingham: PV 31 cp, YP 12. Pore ~9.5 ppg; fracture at Shuaibba (2940-3032 m) 7100-7400 psi.
String: 5in DP (ID 4.276), BHA = 8 x 6.5in DC (~75.6 m) + 2 string stabilizers 8.25in + bit 0.36 m.
Table 5 (RIH at 100 ft/min): 'Surge Min' equals the static hydrostatic head (0.052*9.96*TVD), 'Surge Max' is the transient peak. deltaP = max - min.
Text: raising trip speed 40 -> 80 ft/min adds ~300 psi surge; optimum 80 ft/min; at 80 ft/min through Shuaibba surge = 6110-6300 psi (static ~5070-5230 psi).
These transient peaks (~1000 psi, ~2 ppg) are 5-8x what any steady-state laminar model gives; a Burkhardt-type model is not expected to reproduce them.

cases.source: Pegasus Vertex white paper 'Surge Pressure Prediction for Running Liners' (SurgeMOD), https://linqx.io/white-paper/Surge-Pressure-Prediction-for-Running-Liners.pdf
cases.kind: simulation (SurgeMOD steady-flow with geometry-dependent clinging constant, laminar+turbulent) — narrow-clearance stress case
notes: Vertical well, TD 15000 ft. Riser ID 17.755in to 3500 ft; casing ID 12.715in to 10000 ft; 14.5in OH to 15000 ft.
11 3/4in 60 lb/ft liner (ID 10.772), 5500 ft long, on drill pipe (DP size not stated; 5in assumed). Radial clearance liner/casing 0.4825in.
Mud 11 ppg, PV 20, YP 15. Weak zone at 15000 ft: PP 9.5 ppg, FG 12 ppg.
Closed-ended at 180 ft/min: bottomhole EMW reaches 12 ppg (FG) when liner bottom reaches ~4000 ft (i.e. deltaP >= 0.052*(12-11)*15000 = 780 psi). With auto-fill (TFA 4.91 in2) safe to ~8400 ft.
Annular velocity in the liner/casing gap is ~19 ft/s at 180 ft/min => fully turbulent. QuackPlan's laminar-only Bingham loss will UNDER-predict here; this case documents that limitation.

cases.source: drillingmanual.com worked example (Bourgoyne-style Bingham laminar hand calculation), https://www.drillingmanual.com/surge-and-swab-pressure-calculations-drilling/
cases.kind: hand calculation (laminar Bingham, displacement-only annular velocity)
notes: Casing ID 8.5in to 10000 ft, 8.5in OH to 13000 ft. 7in flush-joint liner 3600 ft on 4.5in DP. Mud 16.6 ppg, PV 38, YP 15. FG 17.0 ppg.
Pipe velocity 93 ft/min (1.55 ft/s). Their result: DP section 110 psi + liner section 168 psi = 278 psi total => ECD 17.13 ppg at 13000 ft (> FG).

Their annular velocities (0.603 ft/s round DP, 1.349 ft/s round liner) come from a 76.8 gpm displacement flow with NO clinging term, so QuackPlan (clinging 0.45 + displacement) will read higher. Useful to show the clinging-constant sensitivity.

measuredPwdSources_paywalled_or_figuresO.ref: Burkhardt (1961) 'Wellbore Pressure Surges Produced by Pipe Movement', JPT 13(6) 595-605, SPE-1546-G
measuredPwdSources_paywalled_or_figuresO.what: The classic field test: single casing joint lowered into a mud-filled hole instrumented with 5 downhole gauges; tables of mud properties and measured vs predicted viscous-drag, inertia and gel-break peaks. Origin of the 0.45 clinging constant QuackPlan uses. OnePetro paywall.

measuredPwdSources_paywalled_or_figuresO.ref: Wang & Liu (1994) 'Dynamic model predicts well bore surge and swab pressures', Oil & Gas Journal, https://www.ogj.com/home/article/17234245/dynamic-model-predicts-well-bore-surge-and-swab-pressures
measuredPwdSources_paywalled_or_figuresO.what: MEASURED downhole surge/swab in a 3354 ft test well (Zhong Yuan field, China): 9 5/8in casing to 3302 ft, 8.5in bit (nozzle equiv. dia 2.03in), 5in DP + 174 ft DCs. Runs: 13.02 ppg PV37/YP20 at 2954 ft; 12.69 ppg PV34/YP15; swab tests 12.60 ppg PV32/YP13 at 2104 and 3037 ft. Measured peaks are in the figures only (free page, digitise the plots); steady-state Burkhardt over-predicted the peak by 64%.

measuredPwdSources_paywalled_or_figuresO.ref: Rudolf & Suryanarayana (1998) SPE-39395 'Field Validation of Swab Effects While Tripping-In the Hole on Deep, High Temperature Wells'
measuredPwdSources_paywalled_or_figuresO.what: Downhole pressure/temperature/trip-speed logs while tripping in deep HT wells (swab on RIH from thermal effects). Paywalled.

measuredPwdSources_paywalled_or_figuresO.ref: Bing, Kaiji et al. (2001/2003) SPE-67717 / SPE-85109-PA 'Field Validation of Transient Swab-Surge Response With Real-Time Downhole Pressure Data'
measuredPwdSources_paywalled_or_figuresO.what: PWD records of swab, surge, reciprocation and pump-on tripping from Alaska and North Sea wells, several hole sizes, WBM/OBM, compared to a transient model. The best measured dataset in the literature; paywalled (SPE Drilling & Completion 18(4) 280-288).

measuredPwdSources_paywalled_or_figuresO.ref: Mohammad, Belayneh, Davidrajuh (2023) 'Physics-Based Swab and Surge Simulations and Machine Learning Modeling of the Field Telemetry Swab Dataset', Appl. Sci. 13, 10252, https://doi.org/10.3390/app131810252 (open access)
measuredPwdSources_paywalled_or_figuresO.what: Norwegian-shelf wired-drill-pipe (NOV DWT) trip-out: 8.5in hole, 1060 m -> 330 m, sensor 67 m above bit, 3373 samples of downhole EMW / bit position / trip speed (Fig. 7). Data Availability: 'Not applicable' — plotted only, not distributed.

measuredPwdSources_paywalled_or_figuresO.ref: Amir et al. (2022) SPE/IADC MPD & UBO Conf. 'Calibrating ECD, Surge, and Swab Models Using Downhole Pressure Measurements...'
measuredPwdSources_paywalled_or_figuresO.what: PWD-calibrated surge/swab models, MPD context. Paywalled.

unavailable: Equinor Volve real-time WITSML logs carry annular pressure/ECD while DRILLING (pumps on, mud-pulse telemetry) but not during trips — mud-pulse PWD is memory-only when pumps are off, so trip surge/swab is not in the public real-time channels.
NLOG, NOPIMS, NDR: end-of-well reports, no PWD trip records.

UiS thesis (Equinor Johan Castberg PWD tripping data, https://uis.brage.unit.no/uis-xmlui/handle/11250/3017906) — repository host did not resolve from this machine; worth retrying manually, the data itself is not public.
